..
The main focus continues to be on persistent dry conditions, with no
significant rainfall in sight. This is well covered in the fire 
weather section below. The trough will act as a focus for showers 
becoming scattered in coverage behind trough passage, but at this 
time, rainfall amounts look to be minimal (less than one quarter of 
an inch). An isolated thunderstorm or two may develop, but, this risk
looks to be relatively low.

Marine...
Mainly moderate winds will persist through Tuesday night, becoming
moderate to fresh for the latter half of the week, when isolated
gusts to 25 knots may develop. This will also allow our current seas
of 4 to 5 feet to increase to 6 to 8 feet by the weekend.

Fire weather...
The subtropical ridge is strengthening to the north, and this will
continue through the remainder of the week, as an area of surface 
high pressure develops near Minamitorishima. This will allow the 
pressure gradient to tighten, with breezy conditions developing 
island-wide during the day Tuesday. Then, breezy conditions will 
persist at higher elevations for the remainder of the week, while 
being more prevalent from late morning through the late afternoon 
hours only for lower elevations.

The KDBI is now 515, which is in the HIGH FIRE DANGER category. Given
the persistent dry conditions, with no significant rains expected
following the trough passage, the breezy conditions will only
exacerbate the potential for wild fires to develop. It's not out of
the question that a Fire Weather Watch may need to be issued during
the daylight hours towards the weekend, if not earlier.

Eastern Micronesia...
A dry pattern is currently in place across eastern Micronesia.
However, this does look to change over the next few days as the
Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) becomes more active over the region.
This will result in an increase in convection across the region,
mainly affecting Pohnpei and Majuro, though Kosrae will see an
increase in showers during the last half of the week into the 
weekend. Even though increased convection is expected, it will, 
unfortunately, not result in a lot of rainfall. Rainfall amounts 
will not be impressive, though model consensus at this time shows an 
average of 2 to 2.5 inches of rainfall through the weekend across 
eastern Micronesia. This will only give a short reprieve, at best, to
the expected drought as we move into the dry season. Therefore, it 
is important to continue to conserve water and catch as much of the 
expected rainfall through the weekend as possible. Dry season is 
rapidly approaching and every wet pattern looks to include less and 
less rainfall. Maintain vigilance and conserve!

An overall benign marine pattern will continue through the week.
However, seas do look to increase toward the end of the week as an
increasing trade swell moves into the region, produced by a
strengthening trade-wind surge, mostly to the north of the forecast
points. Combined seas could reach as high as 8 feet, especially for
Majuro. Winds will gradually increase for Pohnpei, with gentle to 
moderate trade winds expected near the end of the week, with Kosrae
continuing to see light to gentle trades. For Majuro, winds will
become occasionally moderate midweek.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows isolated to low-end scattered showers 
throughout the region. These showers are expected to be short-lived 
with low rainfall totals. Overall, mostly benign weather with few 
intermittent showers are expected throughout the rest of the week.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Yap and Chuuk are abnormally 
dry (D0) while Palau is in a moderate drought (D1). A strong to 
very-strong El Nino remains the dominant climate oscillation, meaning
a possible earlier onset of drought, as well as the continued 
potential for tropical cyclones. Water conservation is highly 
encouraged sooner rather than later, especially as dry season 
approaches. Maintain general storm preparedness and weather 
awareness.

The north swell continues slowly subsiding. Combined seas of 5 to 7
feet are seen across the region. The north swell has shifted to 
northeast a bit early. Seas are forecast to maintain the 5 to 7 feet
through the week. This will keep surf around 7 to 8 feet. Seas and
surf are expected to remain below advisory thresholds of 10 foot 
seas and 9 foot surf. Light to moderate winds are expected to build 
to gentle to fresh for the middle of the week before tapering down to
light to moderate for the weekend.
